# `tract`

What kind of place a tract is: its ground, the maps that stand on it, the travel bands that cross it, its ruin and its glyph (10 §6).

The engine supplies `engine:none`, which may be named bare (04 §4.4).

## Fields

Besides these, a definition takes the [keys every definition carries](README.md#keys-every-definition-carries).

- `tags` (list of [tag](../values.md#tags); optional): Free-form tags.
- `ground` (id of a [`ground`](ground.md), or `null`; optional): What its ground is. Left out, the tract is the realm's own fill up to the surface and nothing else.
- `params` (object, name → [expression](../values.md#expressions); optional): Values for the ground's parameters: each a plain value or an expression.
- `place` (list of object [`TractPlaceDef`](#tractplacedef); optional): The maps that stand on it.
- `ruin` ([`Sited`](#sited), or `null`; optional): What it becomes when ruined (10 §10.2). Carried as written for the package that builds transforms.
- `bands` (list of string; optional): The travel bands that may cross it (11 §13.2), by id as written.
- `glyph` (object [`TractGlyph`](#tractglyph), or `null`; optional): How it is drawn on the region map.

<a id="tractplacedef"></a>
### `TractPlaceDef`

One entry of a tract definition's `place`: a map that stands on every tract of the definition.

- `map` ([`MapPickDef`](#mappickdef); **required**): Which map: an id, or `{ "tag": … }` for any map carrying the tag.
- `at` ([`Sited`](#sited-2); **required**): `[x, y]`: where the map's anchor goes, in cells east and south of the tract's north-west corner.
- `turn` ([`TurnDef`](#turndef), or `null`; optional): How it is turned, as a map's own `place` writes it. Not turned if left out.
- `facing` ([`Sited`](#sited-3), or `null`; optional): In place of `turn`: the way the map's `front` is to face. The map is rotated so that it does.
- `chance` ([`Sited`](#sited-4), or `null`; optional): The chance that it is placed at all, from 0 to 1.
- `params` (object, name → [`Lit`](#lit); optional): Parameters for the map: plain values.
- `order` (whole number, 0 or more, or `null`; optional): Later placements overwrite earlier where they overlap. Its position in the list if left out.

<a id="tractglyph"></a>
### `TractGlyph`

How a tract is drawn on the region map (12 §6.2). A presentation hint: generation carries it and gives it no meaning.

- `ch` (string, or `null`; optional): The character.
- `fg` (string, or `null`; optional): The foreground colour, by name.
- `bg` (string, or `null`; optional): The background colour, by name.

<a id="mappickdef"></a>
### `MapPickDef`

Which map a `place` entry places: one by id, or any that carries a tag.

Written as a map id or `{ "tag": … }`.

Takes (kept with where it was written, and checked when mods load):

- a string: id of a [`map`](map.md)
- an object: object [`TagObject`](#tagobject)

<a id="turndef"></a>
### `TurnDef`

How a nested map is turned: a fixed turn, or whichever fits.

Written as a turn: degrees, `"any"` or `{ "rot": …, "mirror": … }`.

Takes (kept with where it was written, and checked when mods load):

- a string
- an object: object [`TurnObject`](#turnobject)
- an integer

### `Lit`

A plain value written in data: `true`, `3`, `0.5` or a text.

Written as a number, a boolean or a text.

- an integer

<a id="tagobject"></a>
### `TagObject`

A map chosen by a tag rather than by id.

- `tag` (string; **required**): A tag: any map carrying it may be chosen.

<a id="turnobject"></a>
### `TurnObject`

A turn written as an object: quarter-turns clockwise and whether the map is mirrored first.

- `rot` (whole number; optional): Degrees clockwise: 0, 90, 180 or 270. Default 0.
- `mirror` (`true` or `false`; optional): Whether the map is mirrored, east and west swapped, before it is rotated. Default false.

<a id="dir8"></a>
### `Dir8`

One of the eight horizontal directions, in clockwise order from north.

In data a direction is written in `snake_case`: `"north"`, `"south_east"`.

One of:

- `"north"`: Toward `-y`.
- `"north_east"`: Toward `+x` and `-y`.
- `"east"`: Toward `+x`.
- `"south_east"`: Toward `+x` and `+y`.
- `"south"`: Toward `+y`.
- `"south_west"`: Toward `-x` and `+y`.
- `"west"`: Toward `-x`.
- `"north_west"`: Toward `-x` and `-y`.
